flawed_step: Lines 0030-0038 (Step 1 and Step 2), with the consequences asserted at lines 0046, 0048-0049 and 0056: alpha_1 is built only from direct products pi_1 x pi_2 with pi_1 in beta_1, pi_2 in beta_2, yet it is declared to be 'the set of automorphisms of matrix M_(1,2)' and S_1 the generating set of Aut(H_1 U H_2), culminating in the claim <S_(x-1)> = Aut(H).
counterexample: Take H = C_4 with vertex set {1,2,3,4} and edges 12, 23, 34, 41. Partition it into two blocks H_1 = {1,2} (an edge) and H_2 = {3,4} (an edge); R_{1,2} carries the two cross edges 23 and 41, so M_(1,2) is exactly C_4. Every element of gamma_1 is a direct product pi_1 x pi_2 with pi_1 a permutation of {1,2} and pi_2 a permutation of {3,4}, so gamma_1 has at most 4 elements and every one of them maps the block {1,2} onto {1,2} and {3,4} onto {3,4}. Of those four, only the identity and (1 2)(3 4) are automorphisms of C_4 ((1 2) alone sends the edge 23 to the non-edge 13; likewise (3 4) alone sends 23 to 24, a non-edge). Hence alpha_1 has at most 2 elements and <S_1> has order at most 2. But |Aut(C_4)| = 8: the rotation rho = (1 2 3 4) is an automorphism of M_(1,2) (12->23, 23->34, 34->41, 41->12) and it moves vertex 2 of block H_1 to vertex 3 of block H_2, so rho is not a direct product on the blocks and rho is not in alpha_1 nor in <S_1>. So alpha_1 is a proper subset of Aut(M_(1,2)) and <S_1> has index 4 in it, contradicting line 0038 ('alpha_1 is the set of automorphisms of matrix M_(1,2)'), line 0046 ('<S_1> = Aut(M_(1,2))', and 'any pi_a in Aut(H) acting on the vertices of H_1 U H_2 lies in <S_1>' -- rho is such a pi_a and it does not), and line 0049. Taking x = 2 so that H = H_1 U H_2, the terminal claim of line 0056, <S_(x-1)> = Aut(H), fails outright: the algorithm returns a group of order at most 2 instead of Aut(C_4) of order 8. Since line 0012 and line 0061 make the whole isomorphism test rest on actually obtaining generating sets of Aut(H) (and Aut(G)), the argument collapses.
reasoning_summary: The construction is closed under direct products of per-block permutations, so every permutation it ever examines preserves the block partition setwise. The automorphism group of a graph generally contains elements that move vertices across blocks, and those can never appear in gamma_1, alpha_1 or <S_1>. C_4 split into two opposite edges is an explicit instance: the algorithm yields a group of order at most 2 while Aut(C_4) has order 8, with the rotation (1 2 3 4) as an explicit missing generator. The proof asserts equality with Aut(M_(1,2)) at Step 2/3 and with Aut(H) at Step 5 without any argument that cross-block automorphisms are recovered, and the same gap recurs at every iteration since Step 4 again forms direct products of S_1 with beta_3. Secondary problems (alpha_1's defining conditions simultaneously demand M_(1,2)^pi = M_(1,2) and H_1^pi = G_1, which are incompatible unless the blocks are literally equal; the unsupported bound |beta| <= n^3; the reliance on an unspecified oracle) reinforce the verdict but are not needed for it.
verdict_note: Refutation found at the first risky claim; remainder of the proof not audited per method.
